title: A Friend's Call
content:
Shreya looked at Yagnesh with a puzzled expression.

"What did you just say?"

Yagnesh's eyes widened.

Only then did he realize what had slipped out of his mouth.

"N-Nothing!"

He immediately cleared his throat and forced an awkward smile.

"I mean..."

"It's always exciting to meet someone who loves anime too."

"That's what I was trying to say."

Shreya narrowed her eyes slightly.

"Really?"

"I could've sworn I heard a different word."

Yagnesh let out an awkward laugh.

"No... no..."

"You must have heard it wrong."

Although she wasn't entirely convinced, Shreya decided not to tease him any further.

Instead, she smiled and changed the subject.

The two of them continued chatting for a while, discussing their favourite anime, unforgettable characters, and the stories that had inspired them over the years.

Neither of them realized how quickly time had passed.

Suddenly, Shreya glanced at her wristwatch.

"Oh no..."

"I completely forgot."

Yagnesh looked at her curiously.

"What happened?"

"I have an important meeting."

"I need to leave."

She stood up and picked up her handbag.

"It was really nice talking to you, Yagnesh."

Yagnesh smiled warmly.

"It was nice talking to you too."

"I hope we meet again."

Shreya returned the smile.

"I'm sure we will."

With a gentle wave, she walked out of the café.

Yagnesh remained seated for a few more moments.

His eyes remained fixed on the café entrance long after Shreya had disappeared from sight.

A smile slowly spread across his face as he replayed every moment of their conversation.

Her smile...

Her laughter...

And the embarrassing words that had accidentally slipped out of his mouth.

"What is happening to me...?" he whispered to himself with a shy smile.

________________________________________

Meanwhile...

Thousands of kilometers away...

Siddu finally arrived in the peaceful hills of Shimla.

The cool mountain breeze welcomed him as he stood in front of a familiar house.

It was Yashwanth's home.

A faint smile appeared on Siddu's face.

Instead of ringing the doorbell, he quietly took out his phone and dialled Yashwanth's number.

Inside the house, Yashwanth looked at the caller ID and answered the call without realizing that Siddu was standing just outside his door.

"Hello..."

His voice sounded unusually dull.

"How are you, Siddu?"

"It's been such a long time."

"I really miss you, buddy."

A gentle smile appeared on Siddu's face.

"I miss you too."

"I'm doing well."

"How about you?"

The two friends spoke for a few minutes, catching up on work and life.

Then Siddu's tone became serious.

"Yash..."

"Is there something you want to tell me?"

Silence followed.

Yashwanth didn't answer immediately.

After nearly a minute, he let out a quiet sigh.

"There are so many things I want to tell you..."

"But you're in France."

"And I know you can't come all the way to India just for me."

Just then...

The doorbell rang.

"I'll call you back."

Yashwanth walked toward the entrance and opened the door.

The moment he looked outside...

He froze.

Standing before him...

With the same familiar smile...

Was Siddu.

For a few long seconds...

Yashwanth couldn't believe his eyes.

"S-Siddu...?"

Before Siddu could say a word, Yashwanth stepped forward and hugged him tightly.

His eyes became moist.

"Thank you..."

"Thank you for coming."

Siddu smiled and gently patted his friend's back.

"Between friends..."

"There are no 'thank yous'..."

"And no 'sorrys.'"

Yashwanth smiled through his tears and invited him inside.

After Siddu freshened up, the two friends sat together in the living room.

Although five years had passed since they had last met in person, nothing had changed between them.

True friendship had remained untouched by time and distance.

After a brief silence, Yashwanth looked at Siddu.

"What made you come here so suddenly?"

Siddu leaned forward.

"I spoke to Narendra before coming."

"He told me that something had happened."

"But he didn't know the complete story."

Narendra had been one of Siddu and Yashwanth's closest classmates during their engineering days. The concern in his voice had been enough to make Siddu leave France without a second thought.

Siddu looked directly into his friend's eyes.

"Tell me..."

"What happened exactly?"

Yashwanth lowered his head.

Silence filled the room.

After taking a long, shaky breath, he slowly looked up at Siddu.

"It's a long story..."

"...and it changed my life forever."
